## Correction: the `tests` criterion is BLOCKING, and already covers 3 of the 5 proposed shapes

Measured at `origin/main` `4cf1ae42946`. This ticket's description and the parent epic's
Finding 3 both rest on a premise that is no longer true. Recording the measurement before
the scope is settled, so the ticket is not reviewed against a false baseline.

**1. It is blocking, not advisory.** `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`:

```
"tests": {
  "default_posture": "blocking",
  "block_threshold": 0.54,
  "blocking_enabled": true
}
```

The `_comment` on that entry records why: bug `obese-dihedral-ermine` flipped it to
blocking from the code-v4 replay, "blocks 99 changes / 8.0%, operator-accepted." The
epic's text was written 2026-09-07 and predates the flip.

**This ticket's acceptance criterion "The criterion's posture is unchanged by this story.
Verified by a test asserting it is still advisory" is therefore FALSE as written and will
be removed.**

**2. Three of the 5 proposed shapes are already in the rubric**
(`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`):

| Proposed shape | Already covered by |
|---|---|
| pinning refactor mechanics | `change-detector` — litmus names "a private method extracted / the module reorganized, WITHOUT any observable-behavior change" |
| pinning re-export identity | `change-detector` — "asserts an internal name, structure, or intermediate state" |
| pinning import shape | `change-detector`, same clause |

Plus `source-grepping` and `existence-only` are already flagged, and `existence-only` is
described in the rubric as "a change-detector that breaks on a rename."

**3. What is genuinely absent.** Searched the whole 130-line rubric for `expir`, `LOC`,
`line count`, `size cap`, `seam` — the only hits are unrelated words.

- **LOC floor/ceiling pinning** appears nowhere. A test asserting a file stays under N
  lines is not described by any antipattern.
- **Re-running a gate script over the real tree** is currently **VALID**, not flagged.
  Guard (iii) permits greps of command output "provided the producer's liveness is
  established", and the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception explicitly validates a
  `grep`/`awk` over a non-executable instruction artifact. The epic's complaint about
  "around 30 modules re-running lint scripts over the real tree" is therefore a request to
  flag something the rubric currently blesses.
- **Expiry** exists, but only for one shape. Guard (viii) accepts "a strict xfail
  (`strict=True`) whose `reason=` (or an adjacent comment/linked ticket) names a concrete
  removal condition." The concept is present; it is simply not available to a
  mechanics-pinning test.

**Consequence for scope.** Writing all 5 shapes as proposed would restate 3 antipatterns
the rubric already carries. Adding duplicate rubric text inside an epic whose purpose is
reducing complexity would be self-defeating, and `A1`'s NIH facet exists to catch exactly
that. The scope decision is with the operator.

## Shape 3 confirmed as a real, uncovered gap — the other two shapes are not

Measured against `origin/main` at `eba93991965`.

**The rubric says nothing about LOC bounds.** `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md`
is 130 lines; `grep -n "LOC\|line count\|module size\|ceiling\|floor"` over it returns no
match (RC=1). So a new test that hard-codes an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file draws
no finding from the tests criterion today.

**ADR 0058 forbids exactly that.** `docs/adr/0058-the-module-size-limit-file-is-the-only-loc-ceiling.md:26-29`:
"`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is the single authoritative LOC ceiling... No other test
may assert an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file, and none may hard-code a ceiling
value." The ADR also preserves the anti-fragmentation FLOOR (`:31-37`) as explicitly NOT
covered by the prohibition, so a taxonomy that treats "LOC pinning" as one undifferentiated
shape would wrongly flag the floor.

That is a standing project decision with no enforcement in the review path -- the gap this
ticket is actually about.

**The other two shapes in this description do not survive re-measurement**, per the
existing cross-reference comment: the held-out-twin premise names a convention retired
outright by `0b5d004f394` (0 tracked files match `heldout`/`held_out`, epic `6ed2-24e5`
closed), and the ~30 lint-rerunning modules are currently BLESSED by the rubric's guard
(iii) plus the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception, making that a change in the rubric's
judgement rather than a coverage gap.

**Consequence for scope.** This ticket is rescopable rather than obsolete, but to one
narrow shape: teach the tests criterion that a test asserting an upper LOC bound on a
`src/rebar` file, or hard-coding a ceiling value, is a finding -- while explicitly exempting
the anti-fragmentation floor and `test_module_size_contract.py`, which ADR 0058 names as the
single sanctioned mirror. The description's RED PROOF must also replay a guard diff from
git history (e.g. `git show b91f8f6830c`), since all 5 named guard modules are deleted.

## 3 of the 5 named shapes are already in the rubric; 2 are the real gap

Measured against `origin/main` by reading the criterion the ticket proposes to change:
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` (the Pass-1 test-sufficiency overlay; eval spec
at `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`).

The ticket's premise is that "nothing anywhere asks whether a test is pinning BEHAVIOUR or
merely pinning the shape of a refactor." The rubric already asks that, by name:

| Ticket's shape | Rubric today |
|---|---|
| 1. pinning refactor mechanics | **covered** — `change-detector`: "asserts an internal name, structure, or intermediate state; would break on a behavior-preserving refactor", plus Four-Criterion Test (a) *refactoring violation* |
| 2. pinning re-export identity | **covered** — same `change-detector` clause; asserting `a.b is c.d` is an internal-structure assertion |
| 3. pinning a LOC floor or ceiling | **NOT covered** — `existence-only` reaches a bare `test -f <file>` and nothing else; no clause mentions a size bound |
| 4. pinning import shape | **covered** — `change-detector`; and Four-Criterion (a) is the litmus it already applies |
| 5. re-running a gate script over the real tree | **NOT covered, and partly BLESSED** — guard (iii) explicitly validates "greps of COMMAND OUTPUT (stdout/stderr/exit code of the EXECUTED unit)" once producer liveness is established, and Rule-5 validates greps over non-executable instruction artifacts |

Adding all 5 would restate 3 clauses the overlay already carries, in different words, inside
the same prompt — which makes the rubric longer without making it stricter, and creates two
phrasings of one rule that can drift apart. Shape 5 is worse than redundant: it would
CONTRADICT guard (iii) unless the new text carves out the difference between running the unit
under test and running a project gate over the whole tree.

**Shape 3 is the one with an authority behind it and no detector.** ADR 0058 (Accepted; epic
`061c`, ticket `db7f`) decides: "`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is the single authoritative
LOC ceiling... No other test may assert an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file, and none may
hard-code a ceiling value." Nothing enforces it — no reference in `scripts/`,
`.github/workflows/`, or `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`.

Two exemptions the ADR names explicitly, which any detector or rubric clause must preserve:

- **The anti-fragmentation floor is retained** and is NOT covered by the prohibition: "never
  create files < 100 LOC by splitting" guards a failure the cap structurally cannot see,
  because the gate only rejects files that are too large. The ticket's shape 3 says "a LOC
  floor OR ceiling", which would flag the one bound the ADR deliberately keeps.
- **`tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is the sanctioned mirror.** It reads the limit
  from `.github/module-size-limit.txt` via `read_limit()` rather than hard-coding one
  (`test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap`), so it asserts an upper LOC bound by design and
  must not be flagged.

The ADR's own reasoning for why the stricter ceilings were wrong is worth carrying into
whatever lands: they inverted the governance (the locked 800 cap was guarded by an admin
override, while the tighter bounds were bare integer literals any contributor could edit), and
they failed mid-refactor by construction (a multi-commit decomposition passes through states
where the file has grown before it shrinks).

**Consequence for scope.** The defensible change is narrow: teach the overlay that a test
asserting an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file is a finding, with the floor and the
single-sourced mirror exempted. Shapes 1, 2 and 4 are already asked; shape 5 needs a contract
decision against guard (iii) before it can be written at all.

Recorded before the scope is settled so the plan is not written against a false baseline. The
same measurement bears on sibling `d278-3792-6538-4c8e`, whose disposition is with the
operator.

## ADR 0058 is violated 5 times on `origin/main` today — shape 3 has live targets

Measured against `origin/main` (`e1c9eb09fa3a`) from an origin/main-based worktree, not the
main checkout. **That distinction mattered:** `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` sits detached at
`2e28d817a7e`, a tree with 3908 files to origin/main's 3784, and a first scan run there
reported 2 extra violations (`test_signing_module_split.py`, `test_agent_call_seam.py`) that do
not exist on `origin/main`. Any scan for this ticket must run from a worktree, not the main
checkout.

ADR 0058 decides: "`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is the single authoritative LOC ceiling...
No other test may assert an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file, and none may hard-code a
ceiling value." Every assertion below breaks **both** halves — it bounds a `src/rebar` file
*and* hard-codes the number.

| Test | Target | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/unit/test_run_span.py:114` | `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` | `<= 800` |
| `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py:302` | `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` | `<= 800` |
| `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:394` | `src/rebar/reconciler/get_rotation.py` | `100 <= ... <= 500` |
| `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:395` | `src/rebar/reconciler/binding_store.py` | `<= 800` |
| `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:396` | `src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_differ.py` | `<= 800` |

`RECONCILER_DIR` resolves to `src/rebar/reconciler` at `:96`, so all 3 of those target
`src/rebar`.

**Both failure modes ADR 0058 predicted are present.** The 3 bare `800` literals are the
governance inversion: the real cap is administrator-locked in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`,
while these copies are integers any contributor can edit, and an administrator raising the cap
would make 3 tests fail for files that are legitimately inside the new limit. The `<= 500` on
`get_rotation.py` is the mid-refactor failure: a multi-commit decomposition passes through
states where the file has grown before it shrinks.

**The exemptions hold as described.** The `100 <=` lower bound at `:394` is the retained
anti-fragmentation floor and is not a violation. `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` is
the sanctioned mirror — `test_no_src_module_over_the_hard_cap` obtains its cap from
`read_limit()` reading `.github/module-size-limit.txt` (`:34`) and hard-codes nothing, so it
asserts an upper bound by design and must never be flagged.

**Consequence.** Shape 3 is not hypothetical: enforcement has 5 present-day targets, which also
means this ticket's work now has a concrete before/after. It also refutes the "nothing has
reintroduced a violation, so leave ADR 0058 unenforced" disposition — violations exist and
were added after the ADR.

**The change (7 files, matching the declared file_impact):**

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` — added the `loc-ceiling-pinning` antipattern to the recall list, with both ADR 0058 exemptions stated inline (the anti-fragmentation floor; the `read_limit()` single-sourced mirror) and the mixed `100 <= n <= 500` case called out explicitly. Added FP guard (xi) so the fixed forms are not flagged.
- `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — 29 → 33 cases. One recall case (`R-loc-ceiling-pinned-literal`, seeded from the live `test_run_span.py` violation) paired with three no-fire cases: the floor, the `read_limit()` mirror, and a numeric payload budget that is not a file line count (guarding against the antipattern over-generalizing to every `<= N`).

- `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` — new author-facing section under the fail-open material, matching the precedent set by story 3fce.

**The 5 violation sites, cleaned:**

- `tests/unit/test_run_span.py` — `test_gate_dispatch_within_module_cap` deleted wholesale; the whole test existed only to pin `<= 800`.
- `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py` — `test_runner_stays_within_the_module_size_cap` deleted wholesale, same reason.
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py` — the `<= 500` upper half and both `<= 800` assertions removed; the `100 <=` anti-fragmentation floor **retained**, with a comment naming ADR 0058 as the owner of the upper bound. The now-unused `line_counts` dict collapsed to a direct count of the one file the floor applies to.

**The 2 non-violations, untouched** — `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:137` (`len(base) + len(out) <= 500`, a payload budget) and `tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py:93` (`elapsed_ms <= 500`, a wall-clock assertion inside a lint fixture). A post-change tree sweep confirms these two are the only remaining `<= 500`/`<= 800` matches under `tests/` and `scripts/`.

**Verification so far:** `make lint` green (including all three ratchets). `pytest` on the 3 touched modules: 29 passed. `pytest -k "eval_spec or eval_discipline or criteria_routing or overlay or guide"`: 329 passed, 2 skipped. `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD`: OK. The eval spec parses and reports 33 dataset cases.

**Note on the AC design**, repeated here because it is the easiest thing for a later reader to get wrong: there is deliberately **no test asserting the antipattern's text is present in the shipped overlay**. compiled_state.description:
## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, deliverable 4. Rescoped by operator decision 2026-11-02 after
re-measurement collapsed 4 of the 5 original shapes.

## The gap, re-measured on `origin/main` f1fe7c6f587

The original plan named 5 "not a behaviour test" shapes. Measuring each against the live
rubric `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` (130 lines; antipattern list
`:22-71`, false-positive guards `:72-112`) leaves exactly one:

| Shape | Status on `origin/main` |
|---|---|
| 1. pinning refactor mechanics | already flagged — `change-detector` `:23-26` |
| 2. pinning re-export identity | already flagged — `change-detector` `:23-26` |
| 3. **pinning a LOC ceiling** | **not covered — this story** |
| 4. pinning import shape | already flagged — `change-detector` `:23-26` |
| 5. re-running a gate script | BLESSED — Rule-5 `:81-87`, guard (iii) `:88-94` |

Shape 5 is not an oversight: guard (iii) permits greps of command output from an executed unit
when producer liveness is established. Flagging it would contradict rubric text written on
purpose, so it is dropped rather than carried.

Shape 3 is the one real gap, and it has a standing decision behind it.
`docs/adr/0058-the-module-size-limit-file-is-the-only-loc-ceiling.md:26-29` (Accepted) decides:
"`.github/module-size-limit.txt` is the single authoritative LOC ceiling ... No other test may
assert an upper LOC bound on a `src/rebar` file, and none may hard-code a ceiling value."

Nothing detects a violation. `grep -rn 0058 scripts/ .github/workflows/ tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`
returns nothing on f1fe7c6f587, and the rubric names no LOC shape. The rule is written down
and unenforced.

**The 5 live violations**, measured on `origin/main` f1fe7c6f587:

- `tests/unit/test_run_span.py:114` — `<= 800`
- `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py:302` — `<= 800`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:394` — `100 <= ... <= 500`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:395` — `<= 800`
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:396` — `<= 800`

Two nearby hits are NOT violations and must stay green:
`tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:137` (`len(base) + len(out) <= 500`, a token
budget) and `tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py:93` (`elapsed_ms <= 500`, a timing
assertion). Neither bounds a file's line count.

## The change

Add one antipattern, `loc-ceiling-pinning`, to the existing antipattern list in
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md` (`:22-71`); add its paired recall and no-fire
cases to `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`; record the provenance in the
`tests` `_comment` of `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` (no routing VALUE
changes); document the pattern in `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md`; and clean the 5
violation sites. This is the file set 4c57247ff88 used for the fail-open oracle, minus the
`base` overlay, which this shape does not touch.

Every edited file is already in the review path, and no new mechanism is introduced, so the
mechanism-delta ratchet (`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check`, exit 0 on f1fe7c6f587)
stays clean. No new config key, gate, flag, or fixture.

The criterion is already **blocking**, not advisory: `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`
`tests` entry carries `"default_posture": "blocking"`, `"blocking_enabled": true`,
`"block_threshold": 0.54`, flipped by bug obese-dihedral-ermine. The original plan's criterion
asserting "it is still advisory" was false and is removed, not weakened.

**The two ADR 0058 exemptions must be preserved in the rubric text**, or the antipattern will
fire on code the ADR deliberately keeps:

1. The anti-fragmentation **floor** (ADR 0058 `:31-37`): "never create files < 100 LOC by
   splitting" is retained and explicitly not covered by the prohibition. A lower bound is the
   opposite check, not a duplicate one. `test_get_rotation.py:394`'s `100 <=` half is a floor;
   only its `<= 500` half violates.
2. The sanctioned **mirror**, `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`, which reads the limit
   through `read_limit()` rather than hard-coding it. A test that sources the ceiling from
   `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is the ADR's prescribed form and must not be flagged.

## Provider neutrality

Per `project.portability`: the change is rubric prose in a Markdown overlay consumed by the
code-review gate's Pass-1 runner. It names no vendor, model, or tool-calling syntax, and adds
no CI-only trigger — the criterion already runs wherever the code-review gate runs. The eval
spec's `model: anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` pin is the existing calibration corpus's property,
is not read by the gate, and is not changed here.

## Acceptance criteria

Verification is by eval-spec cases, not by grepping the rubric's prose. The rubric's own
Rule-5 litmus (`:84-87`) says a grep that merely guards the author's wording IS a
change-detector, and the precedent commit for this rubric (4c57247ff88, the fail-open oracle
antipattern) touched no `tests/` file for exactly that reason — it paired each seeded recall
diff with a post-fix no-fire case in the eval spec.

- [ ] The `tests` rubric's antipattern list gains a `loc-ceiling-pinning` entry: a test
      asserting an upper bound on a source file's line count, or hard-coding a ceiling value,
      with ADR 0058 named as its authority and both of that ADR's exemptions stated inline
      (an anti-fragmentation LOWER bound; a test that reads the ceiling from
      `.github/module-size-limit.txt` instead of hard-coding it). Verified by the recall and
      no-fire cases below, which cannot pass unless the language is present and correctly
      scoped.
- [ ] RED PROOF: the overlay fires on a diff that adds a hard-coded upper LOC bound. The diff
      is replayed from git history (`git show b91f8f6830c`, which added the now-deleted
      `tests/unit/test_config_resolver_seam.py`) because all 5 originally named seam-guard
      modules are deleted from the tree. Verified by an `R-loc-ceiling-*` case in
      `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml`.
- [ ] NO-FIRE PROOF: the overlay stays silent on (a) a lower-bound-only assertion, (b) a test
      reading the ceiling through `read_limit()` as `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`
      does, and (c) a non-LOC numeric bound — a token budget or an elapsed-milliseconds
      assertion. Verified by three `FP-loc-ceiling-*` cases in the same spec, so the
      antipattern is proven scoped rather than firing on any `<= <int>`.
- [ ] The eval spec still passes its declared gate (`at_least(2)` over 3 epochs,
      `coverage_threshold: 0.8`) with the new cases added. Verified by
      `rebar prompt eval code-review-tests`.
- [ ] All 5 live violations are removed or converted to the sanctioned form:
      `tests/unit/test_run_span.py:114`, `tests/unit/test_header_delivery.py:302`, and
      `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_get_rotation.py:394-396`. The `100 <=` floor at `:394`
      is retained. Verified by the full suite staying green and by no upper LOC bound remaining
      in those files.
- [ ] `tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py:137` and
      `tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py:93` are unchanged. Verified by the diff, so
      the cleanup is proven not to over-reach.
- [ ] The author-facing guide `src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md` (served by
      `rebar explain review`) documents the pattern, as 4c57247ff88 did for the fail-open
      oracle. Verified by reading the rendered guide.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Out of scope

- Changing the criterion's posture or `block_threshold` (already blocking; a threshold change
  is a separate calibration decision needing its own replay evidence).
- The 4 collapsed shapes above.
- A CI script or lint rule enforcing ADR 0058 deterministically. The rubric entry is the
  review-time check; a detector would be a new mechanism and a separate ticket.
